claims.text: MySQL 8.4 documents that InnoDB supports READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, and SERIALIZABLE; its default isolation level is REPEATABLE READ.

MySQL 8.4 documents that READ UNCOMMITTED nonlocking reads can be dirty reads; READ COMMITTED gives each consistent read its own fresh snapshot and normally disables gap locking for locking reads, UPDATE, and DELETE except foreign-key and duplicate-key checks, so phantom-row problems can occur; REPEATABLE READ uses the snapshot established by the first consistent read in a transaction, locks a unique-index unique search as an index record and uses gap or next-key locks for other search conditions; and SERIALIZABLE is stricter, is used mainly in specialized situations such as XA and concurrency/deadlock troubleshooting, and with autocommit disabled implicitly converts plain SELECT to SELECT ... FOR SHARE.

MySQL 8.4 documents that consistent reads use multiversioning to present a point-in-time snapshot; REPEATABLE READ reuses the first consistent-read snapshot within a transaction, READ COMMITTED sets a fresh snapshot for each consistent read, and consistent reads do not set locks on accessed tables.

MySQL 8.4 supports global, session, and next-transaction isolation-level scope. Session-level changes apply to subsequent transactions in that session and do not retroactively change the current transaction; global changes affect subsequent sessions rather than existing sessions.
